Command: A priest with a blemish shall not enter behind the veil
Summary: The command: A priest with a blemish shall not enter behind the veil (Leviticus 21:23). A blemished priest might not go in unto the veil nor come near the altar, lest he profane God's sanctuaries.
Commandment: A priest with a blemish shall not enter behind the veil.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The blemish did not make the priest unclean or unwelcome: he still ate the bread of his God, most holy and holy (Leviticus 21:22). He was barred only from approaching to offer — a visible picture that the offering itself must be unblemished, pointing to the unblemished Lamb (1 Peter 1:19).
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: he shall not profane my sanctuaries, for I the LORD do sanctify them (Leviticus 21:23).
